verification_note: Each value was read twice from its PDF by two independent automated readers on 2026-10-09. The reads agreed on 272 of the 279 rows transcribed (all 279 rows here, including 17 estragole and methyl eugenol rows and 1 methyl N-methylanthranilate row). The 7 disagreements were settled from the PDF's own text lines, where each row reads '<value> <substance CAS> <NCS name>' (checked against Palmarosa oil, 82.4 % geraniol): 5 kept the first read, and Styrax extract (0.1) and Styrax oil, Honduras (0.05) took the second for benzaldehyde. No value has been checked by a person against the printed page. Correct a value by editing its row; every row carries its source PDF. The 7 Cassia oil rows (Cinnamomum aromaticum Nees, CAS 8007-80-5) were added on 2026-10-15 from the same PDFs, each read twice and agreeing. On 2026-10-25 the Annex I tables of six more standards (carvone, alpha-bisabolol, cuminaldehyde, perilla aldehyde, 2-methoxy-4-propylphenol, thujone) were read twice by two independent automated readers from the PerfumersWorld copies of the 2020 (Amendment 49) PDFs; all 126 rows agreed, and the rows for owned naturals were added. Supplier certificate rows (source_kind supplier_ifra_certificate) are not Annex I and were read from Kenny's own PerfumersWorld SKUs.
source: IFRA Standards, Amendment 49 (2020), Annex I 'Contributions from other sources' tables, as copied by PerfumersWorld; one PDF per restricted substance (source_url on every row). Each value is the highest concentration of that substance reported in that natural.
scope: Only the 27 restricted substances with a Category 4 limit in ifra_cat4_51.json, and only rows for naturals Kenny owns and their close variants. Safrole (IFRA_STD_179) has no per-natural table, only its 0.01 % notebox total, so the safrole in nutmeg is not counted. Annexes of other restricted substances were not read.
stock_rule: A stock maps to the NCS rows that are that natural, not its part or species variants. Where the species, part or extraction is uncertain, every candidate is listed and the highest value per substance is used. Rows that print one substance under several CAS numbers (cedrene) also take the highest value, never the sum.

Aurantiol.basis: Aurantiol is the Schiff base of hydroxycitronellal (C10H20O2, 172.27 g/mol) and methyl anthranilate (C8H9NO2, 151.16 g/mol) with loss of water (18.02 g/mol): 305.41 g/mol. 172.27 / 305.41 = 56.4 % of its mass is hydroxycitronellal, counted toward the hydroxycitronellal Category 4 total. The methyl anthranilate share has no IFRA standard of its own.
Aurantiol.source: stoichiometric calculation. IFRA_STD_043 (Amendment 51, read 2026-10-09) sets Category 4 at 2.1 % and does not mention Schiff bases, so counting this share is a conservative project choice, not an IFRA instruction.
